p: praise: Though all the world condemn me, yet you will approve my innocence and that is sufficient praise to me.
but I give myself unto prayer: To declare that I had no other refuge, but you, in whom my conscience was at rest.

Set thou a wicked man over: Whether it was Doeg or Saul, or some familiar friend that had betrayed him, he prays not for private affection, but moved by God's Spirit, that God would take vengeance on him.
prayer become sin: As to the elect all things turn to their profit, so to the reprobate, even those things that are good, turn to their damnation.
office: This was chiefly accomplished in Judas, Ac 1:20.

the extortioner catch all that he: He declares that the curse of God lies on the extortioners, who thinking to enrich their children by their unlawfully gotten goods, are by God's just judgment deprived of all.
Let the iniquity of his fathers: Thus the Lord punishes to the third and fourth generation the wickedness of the parents in their wicked children.
he remembered not to shew mercy: He shows that God plagues them in a strange way who show themselves cruel toward others.
so let it come unto him: Thus the Lord gives to every man the thing in which he delights so that the reprobate cannot accuse God of wrong, when they are given up to their lusts and reprobate minds.
from the LORD: For being destitute of man's help, he fully trusted in the Lord, that he would deliver him.
name's sake: As you are named merciful, gracious and long suffering, so show yourself in effect.
locust: Meaning that he has no stay or assurance in this world.
faileth of fatness: For hunger that came from sorrow, he was lean and his natural moisture failed him.
save me according to thy mercy: The more grievously Satan assailed him, the more earnest and instant was he in prayer.
curse: They will gain nothing by cursing me.
mouth: Not only in confessing it secretly in myself but also in declaring it before all the congregation.
condemn his soul: By this he shows that he had nothing to do with them who were of little power, but with the judges and princes of the world.
